assumptions.note: People, home assignments, routines, budgets and preferences are invented test inputs, shared by both policies.

Choice score = preference − CAD cost × cost sensitivity × cost weight − total minutes / 30 × time sensitivity − shared-with-cars km × safety sensitivity × discomfort, plus fixed seeded variation of width 0.8.
Minutes beyond the 619 m section are fixed per option and do not change with either policy.
Parking and driving costs per trip are illustrative.
Purchase amounts are illustrative; OSM supplies presence only.
A focal shop closes at 18:00 the next period if this sample’s receipts fall below its stated floor; this is not a closure or sales model.
Converts a dollar of fare or parking into choice score before personal cost sensitivity.

assumptions.unit: utility per km shared with cars
assumptions.note: How much riding in a car lane lowers a cyclist’s choice score, before personal safety sensitivity. No observed Toronto removal response.
Off gives the zero-retail-response case: shops keep their hours whatever the receipts.

metric_definitions.label: Cycling distance shared with cars on Bloor (exposure, not injuries)
Household spending at focal Bloor shops
Mean in-section minutes per Bloor cycling leg
Mean in-section minutes per car leg
Focal shops on reduced hours next period

not_estimable.reason: Nineteen synthetic people have no representative weights; section results cannot be scaled to the TTC.
OSM supplies presence only; there is no sales, cost or survival model.
Shared-with-cars distance is exposure; no conflict or injury model is attached.
No fleet, trip-length or substitution emissions model.
Car time is simulated only inside the 619 m section from observed entry flows.
No Bathurst–Spadina construction plan or cost; the City multi-corridor estimate does not apply to this segment.

limitations: Nineteen synthetic people with invented routines and preferences; not a sample of Bathurst–Spadina residents or visitors.
Movement, signals, crosswalks, Line 2 departures and fares are enforced by the mapped sandbox; signal timings are assumed and background traffic follows one observed weekday.
Shop presence comes from OpenStreetMap; baskets, receipts and staffing thresholds are synthetic.
Outputs describe this 619 m section only and must not be scaled to the corridor, TTC or City.
